supported_facts: AP published the article on April 2, 2026.

AP reported that Hegseth had fired more than a dozen top generals and admirals since taking office, and that more than a dozen other senior military leaders had either retired early or been removed from their posts.

The report named Army Chief of Staff Gen. Randy George, Army Gen. David Hodne, and Army Maj. Gen. William Green among leaders affected; it said Pentagon officials did not give reasons for George’s or Hodne’s and Green’s departures.
The report distinguishes firings from early retirements and other removals; it does not say all affected leaders were fired.
quotes: The ouster, reported earlier by CBS News, is just the latest of more than a dozen firings of top generals and admirals by Hegseth since he took office last year.
Since then, more than a dozen other top military generals and admirals have either retired early or been removed from their posts.
A reason for their departures also was not given.
limitations: This article was published April 2, 2026, and does not establish how many leaders had been affected by the frozen record date of November 7, 2025.
It does not provide a case-by-case list for the aggregate counts or establish the exact November 2025 total stated in the staged description.
